title: Miliary and disseminated TB
dek: Hematogenous millet-seed disease is a burden and sanctuary problem: easy to miss on a poor film, easy to under-sample, high TBM overlap. Genomics still needs a specimen.
story: Miliary TB is hematogenous seeding with millet-seed nodules. It is not a separate species. HIV, infants, anti-TNF, and pregnancy are classic hosts. Chest radiograph can be obvious or nearly normal (cryptic miliary). High-resolution CT and a diagnostic chase (sputum, induced, BAL, urine LAM, blood/bone marrow in advanced HIV, CSF if neurologic) beat a single smear.

Disseminated disease overlaps TB meningitis, adrenal TB, and occult pulmonary foci. Treat as disease, not LTBI, even when IGRA is negative (anergy). Steroids follow TBM/pericarditis rules, not a miliary reflex.

WRDs may be trace or negative because each sample is paucibacillary while the body burden is high. That paradox is sampling, not a reason to withhold therapy in a dying patient. Culture still tries; WGS may wait for the bottle.
deep: Unmasking IRIS after ART can present as sudden miliary films. That is still TB, not drug failure by default.
Hepatotoxicity plus miliary is a miserable reintroduction problem — bridge carefully.
Congenital TB is a neonatal disseminated object; treat the mother and the neonate as a pair.
Do not use 3HP as therapy for miliary disease. TPT is for infection without disease.

example.title: Fever, HIV, normal smear, millet CT
example.setup: CD4 32, CT millet, sputum Ultra negative ×2, LAM positive.

steps.title: LAM is a disease test here
steps.body: Start TB therapy; do not wait for a third sputum.

steps.title: Look at the CSF
steps.body: Disseminated plus headache or just low CD4 — TBM changes ART timing.

steps.title: Keep culturing
steps.body: WGS will need a isolate or a better tNGS specimen.

example.takeaway: Miliary is disseminated disease: treat, sample widely, watch the meninges.

check.prompt: Miliary TB should be treated as:
choices: TB disease with a full regimen, not TPT
check.answer: TB disease with a full regimen, not TPT

check.prompt: Ultra-negative sputum in radiographic miliary disease most likely reflects:
choices: Paucibacillary sampling of a hematogenous process
check.answer: Paucibacillary sampling of a hematogenous process
check.why: Keep sampling other sites; LAM/CSF/CT still count.

check.prompt: On the constellation, “not TPT” is weighted because:
choices: Miliary is disease and TPT regimens are under-powered for it
TPT is contraindicated in all HIV
check.answer: Miliary is disease and TPT regimens are under-powered for it

whyWrong.TPT is contraindicated in all HIV: False; TPT is indicated after disease exclusion.
